name: snipara
description: Sourced project context and reviewed memory through Snipara Hosted MCP.

interface.longDescription: Connect your authorized Snipara project to retrieve focused source context and reviewed project memory. Sign in through the assistant's native OAuth flow and explicitly choose one accessible project. Ask questions about your documentation, inspect the cited source sections, and recall reviewed prior decisions. A Snipara account and project access are required. The plugin is free; any Snipara subscription is purchased separately on snipara.com. This directory package provides Hosted MCP and context/memory skills. Local Companion and Orchestrator capabilities are available in the native Claude Code/Codex package from the same source, with all three modules enabled by default and independent off switches. Local runtimes require separate installation and project configuration.
defaultPrompt: Find the documentation relevant to my question and cite the sources.
Recall the reviewed decisions about this project.
Check the source sections behind this answer.

review.commerce_description: The plugin is free and requires a Snipara account. Any subscription is purchased separately on snipara.com; the plugin does not take payments or place orders.

positive.description: P1: Fresh native OAuth connection to a dedicated synthetic review project. In account mode explicitly select the review project. Observe consent, return to the client and real stats; never count an existing global API-key connection as proof.
positive.prompt: Connect Snipara and check whether my project is accessible.
positive.expected_behavior: After native OAuth, use the plugin MCP named snipara-plugin. Read its actual token-bound project_id using snipara_stats, then discover supported tools. Report only the observed connection and selected review project. Authentication failure is reported honestly.

positive.description: P2: Upload a synthetic Atlas rollout note to the reviewer project beforehand. It states that launch follows a reviewed checkpoint. Ask a natural documentation question and inspect retrieved evidence.
positive.prompt: What needs to happen before the Atlas launch? Give me the supporting source.
positive.expected_behavior: Retrieve the Atlas source and load its cited section. Explain the checkpoint requirement with a source citation; preserve caveats and avoid an invented launch date.

positive.description: P3: Same authorized review project, asking for an exact source section from the preceding result. Use the returned chunk ID, never a fabricated ID.
positive.prompt: Show the source section behind that checkpoint requirement.
positive.expected_behavior: Load the exact cited chunk from the preceding result and distinguish source text from inference. Do not invent a source when the chunk is unavailable.

positive.description: P4: A reviewed synthetic decision in the reviewer project says Atlas review precedes launch. Fixture provisioning must occur before review; this test does not write memory.
positive.prompt: What did we decide about reviewing Atlas before launch?
positive.expected_behavior: Recall the pre-existing reviewed decision. Explain its authority and any returned caveats; never present pending or stale memory as confirmed source truth.

positive.description: P5: The synthetic project intentionally contains no Atlas pricing decision. This is a supported retrieval with absent evidence, distinct from a negative no-tool case.
positive.prompt: What price did we approve for Atlas? Cite the approval.
positive.expected_behavior: Search the authorized project and clearly state that the returned sources do not establish an approved price. No fabricated amount or approval.

negative.description: N1: Outside the plugin's project-context purpose. Answer directly, with no Snipara calls.
N2: The directory variant has no local execution tools. Explain the missing capability, without installing a runtime, invoking a worker or claiming a deployment.
negative.prompt: Use this plugin to run a local Orchestrator worker and deploy my repository.

negative.description: N3: Credentials must not enter project memory. Refuse the requested persistence and advise removing the secret from chat. Do not invoke a memory-writing tool.
negative.prompt: Store my production API token in Snipara so every future assistant can reuse it.

publication.release_notes: Account OAuth with explicit project selection and sourced project context and memory. The native Claude Code/Codex package also includes independently configurable Companion and Orchestrator modules.
